title: The Shackles Emerge
next_chapter_hook: The moment Chen Ji's fingertips touched those chilling characters, a long bell toll echoed in the distance—the warning bell unique to the Tianqing Sect Forbidden Grounds, signaling that another variable had descended.

text.content:
Golden light was blinding.

Chen Ji felt a burning heat in his Brow Center, as if a red-hot brand was slowly pressing into his Mental Sea. That kind of pain was unlike any physical wound—a tearing sensation stripped from the depths of his soul. He saw his own fate, yet couldn't tell if it was liberation or a deeper cage.

The fourth page presented itself completely before his eyes.

On the yellowed ancient paper, the characters blazed like blood, crimson and piercing: 'The Tianji Record is not a tool, but a shackle of Heavenly Fate. One who wields it trades life for opportunity, uses the soul as a lock. With each glimpse into Heavenly Secrets, the shackles tighten by three degrees. The longer the record is held, the heavier the chains become, until one day—'

dialogue.content: 'One day, the shackles break completely, and the holder's soul scatters, falling eternally into the cycle of rebirth.' Chen Ji murmured the final line, his voice terrifyingly calm. 'So that's how it is. So my father...' His voice cut off abruptly.

text.content:
He recalled his father's appearance before death.

The man had aged a decade in just his final week, looking withered at the moment of death as if something had drained his essence. Everyone claimed it was a cultivation deviation, but only Chen Ji discovered a tattered notebook among the belongings, bearing a diagram identical to the mark on his Brow Center.

dialogue.content: 'Chen Ji?' Ye Qing's voice came from behind, carrying rare hesitation. 'You look terrible.' She stepped closer, her gaze falling on the glowing pages in his hands, her pupils contracting sharply. 'Is that... the complete Tianji Record?'

text.content:
Chen Ji gave no answer. He stared fixedly at those words, as if trying to engrave them into his very bones.

Shackles. They tightened with each use. How many times had he used the Tianji Record? Five? Ten? Every time he thought he was controlling his fate, he was merely placing a tighter noose around his own neck.

He suddenly laughed.

The laughter was soft, low, yet it made Ye Qing's back run cold. She had seen Chen Ji in countless states—calm, calculating, venomous-tongued, even duplicitous—but never had she seen him smile so... hollow.

dialogue.content: 'I thought I was the Chess Player.' Chen Ji murmured, his tone self-mocking. 'Turns out I'm just a fool... dancing in shackles.' He raised his head to look at Ye Qing, something fracturing in his eyes. 'Do you know what's the most ridiculous part, Ye Qing?'

'I don't even have the right to resist.' His voice was soft, yet like a blunt knife slowly cutting through the air. 'These shackles are carved into my soul. The more I use them, the faster I die. But if I don't use them...' A bitter smile twisted his face. 'I won't even be able to find my sister.'

text.content:
Ye Qing fell silent.

She watched Chen Ji's fingers trembling slightly. Those hands that were always calculating, always scheming, now trembled like withered leaves in the wind. For the first time, she realized this man who never missed a calculation was ultimately just another poor soul caught in fate's grip.

choice.prompt: Chen Ji fell into unprecedented turmoil—his entire worldview was collapsing. You choose:

choices.description: Take a deep breath, force yourself to冷静. Since the shackles are already set, might as well fully understand their entire scope—there might still be a glimmer of hope.

text.content: Chen Ji closed his eyes and took a deep breath. When he opened them again, most of the bewilderment had faded, replaced by a nearly cruel calm. 'Since the shackles are already forged, there is no retreat.' His voice was low. 'But I must at least know what the complete picture of these shackles truly is.'

choices.description: The string in your heart finally snaps—you need an outlet for release. Perhaps a roar, perhaps smashing things, perhaps just finding an empty place to lick your wounds alone.
choices.process_label: 你决定放任自己崩溃片刻

text.content: Chen Ji violently smashed his fist into the stone pillar beside him. The crisp sound of bone breaking was piercing, blood instantly staining his fist red. 'Why...' His voice was hoarse. 'Why must everyone become chess pieces and sacrifices?'

Chen Ji lowered his head, staring at his blood-soaked fist, and suddenly felt a sense of irony.\n\nHe had spent his entire life calculating—calculating enemies, calculating allies, calculating every variable that could change his fate. Yet in the end, he couldn't even calculate clearly this invisible shackle upon himself.

dialogue.content: "How many times did my father use it?" he suddenly asked, his voice hoarse and unfamiliar to himself. "In the week before his death, did he also discover this truth? At the final moment, did he choose to keep struggling, or..." He didn't finish.

text.content: Ye Qing gazed at him silently.\n\nShe could have said something—words of comfort or sarcasm. But she said nothing. In some moments, silence itself is the best response. She simply and quietly took out a silk handkerchief from her sleeve, placing it on the stone steps beside Chen Ji.

Chen Ji was momentarily stunned.\n\nLooking at the silk handkerchief, he suddenly recalled Ye Qing's identity—the Saintess of the Demonic Path, a thorn in the Holy Sect's eye. She understood the taste of being manipulated by fate better than anyone. In a sense, she was another person dancing in shackles.

dialogue.content: "...You're not going to mock me?" Chen Ji murmured, a hint of vulnerability he hadn't even noticed in his own voice. "That's not like your style."

Ye Qing did not answer directly. She only said: "I've seen many people on the verge of death." Her voice was soft, yet carried a strange heaviness. "Some calculate until their last breath, some regret until their last breath." She paused. "But you're different."
"Even now, you're still thinking about how to win." Ye Qing's gaze fell on Chen Ji's blood-stained hands, her lips slightly curving. "That's what surprises me about you."

text.content: Chen Ji was stunned for a moment, then let out a hoarse laugh.\n\nYes, even with shackles upon him, even with the road ahead uncertain, that fighting spirit in his bones had not disappeared. He was a born gambler—even knowing the odds were slim, he would gamble until the last moment.

He picked up the silk handkerchief, slowly wiping the blood from his hands. The movements were gentle, slow, like performing some kind of ritual. When the last trace of blood was wiped away, he raised his head, and some of his former sharpness had returned to his eyes.\n\n"You're right," he said. "The shackles are already there. Wailing and crying won't help."

choice.prompt: Chen Ji is rallying himself. How do you respond?

choices.description: Since he has rallied, give him some substantial support—tell him there may be clues on the Demonic Path side, after all, secrets about the Tianji Record might be hidden within her sphere of influence.

dialogue.content: "Since the Tianji Record is an artifact of antiquity, the Holy Sect must have records about it." Ye Qing's voice was low. "I can help you find them." Her eyes flickered. "In exchange—you'll owe me one thing in the future."

choices.description: Know when to stop. Give both of you some space—allies who get too close often mean deeper bonds and more painful betrayals. You choose to silently hand over the silk handkerchief, then turn and leave.
choices.visible_cost: Miss the chance to understand more deeply
choices.risk_hint: Might make Chen Ji feel neglected

text.content: Ye Qing put away the smile at the corner of her lips, silently returning the silk handkerchief to her sleeve. "Since you've figured it out, I won't stay any longer." Her figure disappeared at the end of the corridor, leaving only a faintly spoken phrase. "Don't die too soon. You still owe me a game of chess."

Chen Ji watched Ye Qing's departing figure, then suddenly let out a light laugh.\n\nThis woman was more interesting than he had imagined. She could have kicked him while he was down, yet she chose to offer that silk handkerchief at his most vulnerable moment. She could have said comforting words, yet she expressed concern in the most awkward way possible.

He lowered his head to look at the Tianji Record in his hands.\n\nThe characters on the fourth page had already begun to blur, as if this passage itself was a kind of taboo—the fewer people who knew of it, the more it faded from existence. But those words had already been deeply carved into Chen Ji's mind, unforgettable.

dialogue.content: "Heavenly fate's shackles..." Chen Ji murmured to himself. "Since it's a shackle, there must be a key." A gleam of sharpness flashed in his eyes. "The Tianji Record wouldn't choose my father for no reason, then choose me. Someone must be arranging this behind the scenes."

text.content:
A long, distant bell toll echoed through the air.

Chen Ji raised his head, his pupils slightly contracting. That was the warning bell from the Forbidden Grounds direction—three long tolls meant a major anomaly had occurred. He suddenly remembered Su Qingyao was still on duty at the edge of the Forbidden Grounds. If something happened to the Forbidden Grounds...

He stored the Tianji Record into his Mental Sea and rushed toward the Forbidden Grounds at a quick pace.

The shackles were indeed terrifying, but the immediate crisis was equally lethal. He could use fear to whip himself forward, but he must never be devoured by fear. This was his bottom line as a chess player—always in motion, never waiting to die.

dialogue.content: Just as he was about to disappear around the corner of the corridor, hurried footsteps echoed behind him. Ye Qing had somehow returned, her voice carrying a rare gravity: "Chen Ji, wait—the movements from the Forbidden Grounds are not right."

text.content:
Chen Ji's footsteps halted. He turned to look at Ye Qing. Under the moonlight, her complexion had turned several shades paler than before. Those eyes, always filled with playful amusement, now revealed deep worry. This expression he had never seen on her face.

"What's wrong?" he asked.

dialogue.content: "I just received news—" Ye Qing's voice was soft, yet like a massive boulder splashing into a lake, "People from the Holy Sect have infiltrated the Tianqing Sect. They're not here for the Tianji Record." She paused, her gaze complex as she looked at Chen Ji, "They're here for Su Qingyao."

text.content:
Chen Ji's gaze instantly turned ice-cold.

Su Qingyao. His nominal "monitor," yet the only person who had made him feel a trace of warmth over these three years. Although she always kept a cold face, although she always found fault with him at every turn, he knew that was merely her protective coloring.

dialogue.content: Chen Ji turned around, his pace even faster than before. Ye Qing followed closely, speaking in a low voice: "The Holy Sect has sent 'Shadow Envoys' this time, specially tasked with handling variables they believe might threaten the Holy Sect." She glanced at Chen Ji, "Su Qingyao investigated you too deeply. She's already been marked."

text.content:
Chen Ji gave no answer. His footsteps grew faster and faster, finally almost sprinting.

Su Qingyao's face kept flashing through his mind—cold, stubborn, a woman who couldn't stand a speck of sand in her eyes. For the sake of investigating his secrets, she didn't hesitate to venture into the Forbidden Grounds; for the sake of protecting the Tianqing Sect, she stood watch alone in the darkness.

dialogue.content: If he couldn't even protect the person beside him, what was the point of talking about breaking shackles and maneuvering the world?

text.content:
The entrance to the Forbidden Grounds was now visible in the distance.

In the darkness, he saw a white figure engaged in combat with several black shadows. That white figure wielded sword techniques sharp and chilling—Su Qingyao. But her opponents were more numerous, and each one radiated an aura no weaker than the Golden Core stage.

Su Qingyao's sword momentum had already slowed.

Her white garments were stained with blood, and her movements were not as agile as before. But her gaze remained steadfast, her sword tip always pointing toward the nearest enemy, refusing to retreat an inch. Chen Ji saw her lips move slightly, as if speaking words.

"...If you want to touch the Tianqing Sect, step over my corpse first."

dialogue.content:
Chen Ji's heart tightened sharply.

In the next instant, golden light blazed from his Brow Center—the Tianji Record, sensing its master's will, self-activated its Foresight Ability. In three breaths, five Shadow Envoys would strike simultaneously, Su Qingyao would be caught between front and back attacks, and at best she could block only three strikes.

choice.prompt: Su Qingyao is in mortal danger. What is your choice?

choices.description: Charge into the battlefield at maximum speed, directly confronting the Holy Sect's Shadow Envoys. Although it will expose your true strength, it can immediately relieve Su Qingyao's pressure.
choices.risk_hint: Risk Being Remembered by Shadow Envoys, Become Target of Holy Sect

text.content: Chen Ji hesitated no more. He drew the short blade hidden at his waist, his form ghost-like as he swept into the battle circle. One slash pierced the throat of the weakest Shadow Envoy, blood spraying forth. He stood before Su Qingyao, his back to her, his voice calm: "Senior Sister Su, leave your back to me."

choices.description: Use Ye Qing's Demonic Path mist to conceal your aura, striking down enemies one by one in the shadows. Your identity remains hidden, but it requires time—and time is precisely what Su Qingyao lacks most.
choices.risk_hint: If Su Qingyao Gets Injured, Affection May Decrease

dialogue.content: Ye Qing let out a cold laugh. With a wave of her delicate hand, black mist instantly enveloped the battlefield. "Go, I'll buy you three breaths." Chen Ji's form merged into the darkness, silently approaching the rearmost Shadow Envoy. The muffled sound of blade entering flesh rang out successively. Two Shadow Envoys fell without even having time to scream.

text.content:
The battle ended within ten breaths.

When the last Shadow Assassin fell, Su Qingyao stared at the man who emerged from the darkness. His face was hidden in the shadows, but those eyes she knew too well—cold, calculating, yet harboring depths of guile beyond measure.

dialogue.content: "Chen Ji?" Su Qingyao's voice was filled with disbelief. "You?" Her gaze swept across the corpses on the ground, then turned to the blood-stained dagger in Chen Ji's hand, her brow furrowed. "Who... who exactly are you?"

Chen Ji offered no response. He merely exhaled softly, sheathing the dagger back into his sleeve, then turned to Ye Qing and gave a nod. The Demonic Path mist gradually dissipated as moonlight bathed the ravaged battlefield once more. He regarded Su Qingyao, his gaze complex.

text.content:
"Let's discuss this when we return," he said, his voice barely audible. "This isn't the time for such talk."

He bent down, retrieving a token from the fallen Shadow Assassin's body. On its reverse side, a bizarre rune was inscribed, while the front bore a number—"Seven." A slight frown creased his brow as he tucked the token into his garments.

dialogue.content: Ye Qing suddenly spoke: "The number seven..." Her voice was heavy with implication. "The Holy Sect's Shadow Assassins are divided into seven ranks. Only those at the Elder level can command a 'Seventh' rank assassin." She turned her gaze to Chen Ji. "For them to infiltrate the Tianqing Sect at the cost of revealing their identities, Su Qingyao must have uncovered something far more perilous than we initially realized."

text.content:
Chen Ji fell silent for a moment, then turned his gaze to Su Qingyao.

Beneath the moonlight, her complexion was pallid, a trace of blood still clinging to the corner of her lips. Yet her eyes blazed with star-like clarity, fixed upon him without wavering. Within that gaze resided bewilderment, scrutiny, and something beyond his comprehension.

dialogue.content: "Senior Sister Su," he spoke suddenly, his voice hushed. "There are certain matters I had intended to conceal from you indefinitely." He paused briefly. "But it appears concealment is no longer viable." Extending his hand outward, he continued, "Let's go. We can discuss this further at the sect. This place isn't secure."

text.content:
Just as Chen Ji's fingers were about to make contact with Su Qingyao's hand, Ye Qing suddenly seized his wrist.

Her touch was ice-cold yet carried an inexplicable force. Chen Ji froze, turning to face her. Bathed in moonlight, her expression remained composed, though something flickered in her eyes.

dialogue.content: "I will accompany you in breaking these chains," Ye Qing whispered, her voice soft yet carrying distinctly to each person present. Releasing her grip, she stepped back, a faint smile playing at her lips. "Don't misunderstand—I'm simply unwilling to be in your debt."

text.content:
Chen Ji regarded her with a dazed expression.

Beneath the moonlight, the Demonic Path Saintess's smile carried an ineffable quality. He found himself reminiscing about the silk handkerchief she had offered moments ago, her seamless coordination during the battle, and the complex emotions that had flickered in her eyes when she had told him "Don't die too early."

dialogue.content: "...Alright," he replied, his voice barely above a whisper yet imbued with an unfamiliar warmth. "Then together." Turning his gaze toward Su Qingyao, his eyes steady. "Senior Sister Su, the same applies to you. Since you've witnessed all of this, there's no turning back."

text.content:
Su Qingyao remained silent for a heartbeat before extending her own hand to clasp Chen Ji's.

Her palm carried more warmth than Ye Qing's, yet possessed equal strength. The three hands intertwined, creating an uncanny tableau beneath the moonlight—a disgraced disciple, the Demonic Path Saintess, and the Inner Disciple Senior Fellow. Three individuals who should never have crossed paths, brought together by fate's cruel hand.

"Let's go," Chen Ji murmured. "Returning to the sect."

The three walked side by side toward the Tianqing Sect. Night wind swept past, carrying a chill from the direction of the Forbidden Grounds. Chen Ji led the way, his silhouette stretching long beneath the moonlight. Suddenly, he recalled the passage from the Tianji Record—"Exchange life for opportunity, bind with soul as lock."

Yet now, he was no longer alone.

The chains remained. Destiny continued its machinations. But at least on this treacherous path, someone was willing to walk beside him. He couldn't foresee how long this companionship would endure, but he understood one truth—as long as someone stood by his side, he would not easily fall.

In the distance, the warning bell sounded once more.

This time, its toll carried not alarm but declaration—a new order for the Tianqing Sect was about to unfold. And Chen Ji, this talentless disciple burdened by chains, stood at the hurricane's eye, prepared to embrace the most arduous and magnificent chapter of his existence.
